sentences.text: The animal is known mainly from a single skull and thick skull roofs measuring 22 cm, with estimates of its length at 4.5 meters and weight between 370 and 450 kilograms.
Pachycephalosaurus was a bipedal herbivore with long strong legs and small five-fingered hands.
It possessed a large bony dome on its skull up to 25 cm thick that cushioned its brain.
The bony spikes on the snout were likely blunted rather than sharp.
Pachycephalosaurus wyomingensis is the only known species in the extinct genus Pachycephalosaurus.
This animal is a marginocephalian dinosaur belonging to the family Pachycephalosauridae.
It is the largest known pachycephalosaur, distinguished by an extremely thick, slightly domed skull roof.
Some estimates suggest it reached lengths of 4.5 to 5 meters and weighed up to 2000 kilograms.
Research found that 22% of examined domes had lesions consistent with osteomyelitis, supporting the use of domes in combat.
Fossils have been found in Montana, South Dakota, Wyoming, and Alberta.

The genus Pachycephalosaurus was established by Brown and Schlaikjer in 1943.

In 2007, researchers proposed that related genera Stygimoloch and Dracorex were juvenile or female forms of Pachycephalosaurus.
Pachycephalosaurus gives its name to Pachycephalosauria, a clade of herbivorous ornithischian dinosaurs that lived in the Late Cretaceous.
The genus Tylosteus is considered synonymous with Pachycephalosaurus.
The animal lived during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in western North America, shortly before the Cretaceous–Paleogene extinction event.
It lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Maastrichtian stage, between 68 and 66 million years ago.
